messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: Enterprise-X (VPC, dedicated pool) - missing traces/partial logs for tenant entx-641 across multiple pods — severity P1. Paging @emma-oncall and @raj. Collecting initial context...

emma-oncall: on it. any customer impact reported?

raj: They reported traces dropping around 22:13 UTC and missing logs for inference jobs. Metric dashboards show p95 error increased and trace-sample count dropped to ~10% for that tenant.

sylvie: adding context — Dedicated pool has been running an egress proxy update rolled out during the 21:50 window. Could be a rate/queue misconfig on the forwarder that evicts per-tenant spans.

kai: I can check forwarder health and per-tenant queue lengths. Running check on forwarder pods in entx dedicated namespace: 
```bash
kubectl -n entx-dedicated get pods -l app=egress-forwarder -o wide
kubectl -n entx-dedicated logs $(kubectl -n entx-dedicated get pods -l app=egress-forwarder -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') --tail=150
```

ops-bot: FYI deployment 2023.11.8-proxy started rolling at 21:48 UTC, completed 21:59 UTC. Canary traffic ramped during that window.

emma-oncall: tl;dr: customer is impacted, traces missing (critical for debug), logs partial. Need temporary read access for SRE to EntX log cluster and a safe mitigation path (fallback route to old forwarder).

raj: quick findings: forwarder logs show repeated backpressure errors with per-tenant buffer eviction: 
```
2023-12-05T21:54:12Z WARN tenant=entx-641 buffer: evicted 102 spans due to quota_exceeded (rate=120/s)
2023-12-05T21:54:12Z ERROR tenant=entx-641 egress: http 502 from egress-proxy
```

sylvie: that matches a bad token bucket config on the new proxy. Eviction is per-tenant when burst limit exceeded. The dedicated pool has lower configured burst for enterprise tenants compared to hosted.

emma-oncall: we need to confirm whether this is config or code. Can we flip the proxy to fallback mode routing entx traffic to the previous version? What are rollback implications?

kai: rollback possible but will trigger a short reconnection storm. Alternative: bump the rate limit for tenant entx-641 in the proxy config map and reload proxy, which is lower-impact. I can apply a hotpatch if SRE approves.

emma-oncall: do it. raj please prepare the hotpatch steps and ETA. I will notify customer liaison.

raj: hotpatch plan: 1) update cm entx-egress-burst -> from 120/s to 600/s for tenant id map 2) kubectl -n entx-dedicated rollout restart daemonset/egress-proxy 3) monitor forwarder logs and raw trace ingress. Rolling restart expected ~60s per node. ETA ~8-12m.

sylvie: note: metric retention and index mapping on our trace ingest cluster show partial write errors at 21:54 — we need to re-ingest dropped spans if available in forwarder local cache. Forwarder has local disk cache path /var/cache/egress/entx-641 which may contain evicted spans.

emma-oncall: assign tasks: @kai apply config bump, @raj watch logs & re-ingest, @sylvie coordinate cache pull. I'll update incident channel and page customer success.

kai: applying config now. patch: 
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: entx-egress-burst
data:
  tenant_entx-641: "600"
```
kubectl -n entx-dedicated apply -f entx-burst-cm.yaml && kubectl -n entx-dedicated rollout restart daemonset/egress-proxy
```

deploy-bot: rollout restart invoked for daemonset/egress-proxy at 22:02:43 UTC.

raj: seeing immediate reduction in buffer eviction logs. sample: 
```
2023-12-05T22:03:07Z INFO tenant=entx-641 buffer: accepted 512 spans burst=450/600
2023-12-05T22:03:09Z INFO tenant=entx-641 egress: http 200 to trace-collector
```

emma-oncall: good. can we replay cached spans to restore missing traces? What's the safe re-ingest window?

sylvie: forwarder cache contains files timestamped 21:52-21:56. We'll pull them via scp to a temporary reingest pod that validates deduplication keys before pushing to collector. Pipeline: 
1) scp from forwarder:/var/cache/egress/entx-641/*.ndjson -> s3://replay-temp/entx-641/
2) run validator -> dedupe -> POST to collector /v1/spans/replay

kai: starting cache pull. Using rsync with --progress and gzip stream: 
```bash
ssh ops@forwarder-node-3 'tar czf - -C /var/cache/egress entx-641' | aws s3 cp - s3://replay-temp/entx-641/replay-20231205.tar.gz
```

ops-bot: note - reingest requires rate-limiting to avoid flood. We'll throttle to 2000 spans/s and monitor ingestion lag.

raj: reingest started at 22:08 UTC. Initial subset shows traces restored for recent failed requests. Customer reported first signs of visibility returning.

emma-oncall: customer success updated EntX with interim note: "We've applied an egress rate increase for your tenant and are replaying buffered spans to recover missing traces. No change required on your side." They asked for ETA for full restore.

sylvie: estimate 30-45m to complete replay for 30GB of cached spans at throttle. We'll provide progress updates every 10m.

kai: monitoring dashboards: trace ingestion rate for entx-641 back to baseline ~98% within 3m of hotpatch. Logs streaming resumed.

emma-oncall: transition plan: once replay completes and we confirm stability, we'll schedule a follow-up to harden proxy config (increase default burst for enterprise dedicated pools) and add a canary rule that rejects canary change if per-tenant eviction > 0.

raj: postmortem - temporary action items: 
- revert to stricter burst after analysis? probably increase defaults permanently.
- add per-tenant alert that pages when eviction rate > 0 for >5m.
- add automated cached-spans reingest playbook.

kai: note on safety: we throttled reingest and validated dedupe IDs; no duplicates observed so far.

ops-bot: incident cleared to monitoring state at 22:34 UTC — visibility restored, no client-side action required.

emma-oncall: handing off to sylvie for next-day postmortem and customer comms. @sylvie please own communication and timeline. I'll go OOO shortly but will be available if needed.

sylvie: acknowledged. I'll pull metrics, logs, and the reingest manifest and publish a runbook update tomorrow.

emma-oncall: closing the page. Great job everyone. :clap:
